pack_metadata.title: Incorporate an Indian company, hire the first employee, and complete initial Central compliance
pack_metadata.user_outcome: A qualifier-driven route from company choices to incorporation, first employment and the first applicable Central filings and remittances.
pack_metadata.central_scope: Companies Act incorporation and early filings; PAN, TAN, salary TDS and conditional GST; current labour-code status; EPFO and ESIC threshold decisions and operational filings; Central POSH baseline; necessary regulated/private actors.
explicit_exclusions: Shops and Establishments registration is a state or local branch, never a national procedure.
Professional tax, labour welfare fund, trade licence, municipal permissions and local establishment registrations are state or local branches.
State stamp duty on incorporation, lease instruments, employment instruments or share certificates is not stated as a national amount.
State minimum wages, leave, working-hours and employment-document rules are not generalised nationally.
Sector licences, foreign-investment approvals and regulated-business approvals are excluded unless a qualifier activates a separate specialist route.

qualifying_questions.question: Which company form is intended?
qualifying_questions.why_it_matters: Member and director minima and some post-incorporation duties differ for a one-person, private or public company.
qualifying_questions.blocking_logic: Do not prepare constitutional documents or select a SPICe+ subtype until the intended form is known; Section 8 and producer-company answers leave this bounded demo route.

qualifying_questions.question: How many proposed members and directors are there, and which directors satisfy the India-stay rule?
qualifying_questions.why_it_matters: The Companies Act sets form-specific minima and requires at least one resident director by the statutory stay test.
qualifying_questions.blocking_logic: Block filing if the selected company form lacks the minimum members/directors or no proposed director satisfies the residence condition.

qualifying_questions.question: Is any subscriber/director foreign, or is the activity regulated, non-profit, producer-company, financial, defence, telecom or otherwise approval-sensitive?
qualifying_questions.why_it_matters: These facts can change attachments, authentication, approvals and the competent authority.
qualifying_questions.blocking_logic: Any answer other than No requires a specialist route before the standard demo path is used.

qualifying_questions.question: What state and full address will be the registered office, and is it the same as the correspondence address at incorporation?
qualifying_questions.why_it_matters: The Registrar jurisdiction, office evidence, state stamp duty and whether INC-22 follows incorporation depend on this answer.
qualifying_questions.blocking_logic: Block filing until lawful occupation evidence, owner consent when applicable and a recent utility bill are available; route a different correspondence address to INC-22 within 30 days.

qualifying_questions.question: What are the authorised and subscribed share capital and each subscriber's allocation?
qualifying_questions.why_it_matters: This drives MOA data, subscription funding, commencement declaration and state-linked fees/stamp duty.
qualifying_questions.blocking_logic: Block filing until allocation is internally consistent; do not quote a fee or stamp amount until the live portal calculates it for the state and capital.

qualifying_questions.question: Reserve the name separately in SPICe+ Part A or submit Part A with Part B?
qualifying_questions.why_it_matters: A separate Part A permits two proposed names while an integrated submission permits one and changes sequencing.
options: Integrated Part A and Part B
qualifying_questions.blocking_logic: If Unknown, choose deliberately before submission; do not promise approval or reuse a reserved name after its validity expires.

qualifying_questions.question: Which bank currently offered in the live AGILE-PRO-S form will receive the account application?
qualifying_questions.why_it_matters: A bank-account application is integrated, but the selectable bank list and post-submission KYC route are volatile.
qualifying_questions.blocking_logic: Do not name a bank from an archived list; select from the live form and obtain that bank's current KYC instructions.

qualifying_questions.question: What supplies will the company make, from which states, through which channels, and what current/expected aggregate turnover and compulsory-registration triggers apply?
qualifying_questions.why_it_matters: GST registration is optional in AGILE-PRO-S unless the case is liable; thresholds and compulsory triggers depend on activity and place of supply.
qualifying_questions.blocking_logic: Do not mark GST required or not required until section 22 turnover, section 23 non-liability/exemptions and every section 24 compulsory category are matched to the actual activity, locations and current notifications.

qualifying_questions.question: Is the person an employee, director-employee, contractor, apprentice or another category?
qualifying_questions.why_it_matters: Payroll, wage, TDS, EPF, ESI and state employment rules depend on the real relationship, not its label.
qualifying_questions.blocking_logic: Block payroll onboarding until the relationship is classified from actual facts.

qualifying_questions.question: In which state(s) will the employee ordinarily work, including remote work, and what is the establishment's total worker/person headcount?
qualifying_questions.why_it_matters: State/local employment law and Central OSH, EPF, ESI and POSH thresholds depend on location and count.
qualifying_questions.blocking_logic: Do not apply a state rule nationally or assume that MCA-issued EPFO/ESIC identifiers mean contribution liability.

qualifying_questions.question: Is any employee engaged in a Central-notified hazardous or life-threatening occupation?
qualifying_questions.why_it_matters: ESI may apply even with one employee in a notified hazardous or life-threatening occupation.
qualifying_questions.blocking_logic: Unknown prevents a no-ESI conclusion below the ordinary 10-person threshold.

qualifying_questions.question: What is the employee's basic wages plus dearness allowance, and do they have a prior UAN or prior EPF membership?
qualifying_questions.why_it_matters: Once establishment coverage exists, the Employees' Provident Funds Scheme, 2026 entry-wage, prior-membership and higher-wage provisions determine enrolment.
qualifying_questions.blocking_logic: If EPF coverage applies, do not exclude a person solely because current pay exceeds the entry ceiling when prior membership may continue.

qualifying_questions.question: What are the employee's ESI wages, disability status and work location?
qualifying_questions.why_it_matters: Individual ESI coverage depends on establishment coverage, notified geography/benefit operation and a current Chapter IV wage-ceiling notification; Rule 19 now separately governs disability employer-share relief.
qualifying_questions.blocking_logic: Do not use superseded Rule 50 or the legacy FAQ as the current ceiling. Locate the operative Chapter IV wage-ceiling notification and verify the notified area/benefit date before deciding individual eligibility.

qualifying_questions.question: What salary is projected for Tax Year 2026-27, what declarations/evidence has the employee supplied, and is tax estimated to be payable?
qualifying_questions.why_it_matters: From 1 April 2026 salary withholding is under section 392 of the Income-tax Act, 2025 and the amount is based on estimated salary income.
qualifying_questions.blocking_logic: Do not invent a TDS amount; obtain payroll evidence and compute under the current Act before each payment.

qualifying_questions.question: How many workers are at each workplace, and what current District Officer/Local Committee route serves it?
qualifying_questions.why_it_matters: A workplace below 10 workers uses the Local Committee complaint route, while larger workplaces require an Internal Committee; employer prevention duties still apply.
qualifying_questions.blocking_logic: Do not invent a national Local Committee contact; resolve it with the relevant district/state authority before publishing the workplace route.

tasks.title: Qualify the entity, people, activity, capital and jurisdiction
tasks.user_goal: Select a legally plausible company route and expose specialist branches before spending money.
tasks.trigger: The user intends to incorporate a company in India.
steps: Answer all qualifying questions.
Check minimum members/directors and resident-director condition.
Stop and route foreign, Section 8, producer-company or regulated-sector facts to a specialist.
tasks.tracking: Maintain a dated decision record with unresolved answers marked Action Required.
tasks.rejection_handling: If facts do not satisfy the chosen form, change the company form or people/capital plan before filing.
tasks.escalation: Use a practising company secretary, chartered accountant, cost accountant or advocate for non-standard facts.

state_local_dependency.description: Registered-office and employee-work state activate state/local branches.

tasks.fail_closed_note: Unknown or approval-sensitive facts block the standard path.

tasks.title: Obtain digital signatures and prepare MCA user access
tasks.user_goal: Enable the proposed subscribers/directors and professional to sign and submit the incorporation forms.
tasks.trigger: The individual signatories and professional are known.

fees_duties.label: Digital-signature provider fee
fees_duties.applicability: Varies by licensed certifying authority and assurance/KYC route.

steps: Select a currently licensed certifying authority.
Complete its identity/KYC route.
Register the appropriate MCA business-user roles and associate the valid DSC as required by the live portal.
tasks.tracking: Track certificate validity and MCA association separately.
tasks.rejection_handling: Correct identity mismatch or expired/revoked certificate with the issuing authority before retrying.
tasks.escalation: Use the certifying authority's support first; use MCA help only for MCA account/association errors.

state_local_dependency.description: No state/local procedure is asserted.

tasks.fail_closed_note: No exact provider, price or issuance time is asserted.

tasks.title: Reserve the name or prepare the integrated name request
tasks.user_goal: Obtain a usable proposed company name for incorporation.
tasks.trigger: Company subtype, objects and proposed names are settled.

timelines.label: Approved name reservation validity
timelines.value: 20 days from approval for a new company
timelines.applicability: When Part A is filed separately and the name is approved.

timelines.label: Name-defect rectification
timelines.value: Within 15 days when the Registrar allows resubmission
timelines.applicability: SPICe+ name webform returned under Companies (Incorporation) Rules rule 9.

steps: Choose separate Part A or integrated Part A plus Part B.
Search and justify proposed names against objects and restricted words.
Submit through SPICe+ and retain SRN/approval or resubmission notice.
If returned for a name defect, rectify within the rule 9 fifteen-day window shown in the notice.
tasks.tracking: Use the MCA SRN/status route and record reservation expiry.
tasks.rejection_handling: Read the exact similarity/trademark/object objection and rectify within the rule 9 fifteen-day resubmission window when allowed; after rejection or expiry, start the appropriate fresh route rather than reusing the expired approval.
tasks.escalation: Escalate portal failures through MCA help; seek trademark/name advice for substantive conflicts.

state_local_dependency.description: Name processing is Central; state choice may affect ROC jurisdiction but not a separate state name filing.

tasks.fail_closed_note: Approval is not guaranteed; the separate Candidate money gate t23 controls any live charge.

tasks.title: Prepare the SPICe+ incorporation evidence and constitutional documents
tasks.user_goal: Create a complete, internally consistent filing pack.
tasks.trigger: Entity, people, office, objects and capital decisions are final.

fees_duties.label: Professional/private preparation fee
fees_duties.applicability: Private commercial term, not a government fee.

timelines.label: Utility bill recency
timelines.value: Not older than two months
timelines.applicability: Registered-office utility evidence in the SPICe+ FAQ.

steps: Draft MOA objects and AOA for the chosen subtype.
Prepare declarations/consents and subscriber/director identity and address evidence.
Prepare office title/occupation proof, owner NOC where applicable and recent utility bill.
Cross-check names, PAN/passport data, capital and share allocation.
tasks.tracking: Use a document checklist linked to each webform field and signatory.
tasks.rejection_handling: Correct the underlying document; do not alter private facts merely to bypass validation.
tasks.escalation: Use the certifying professional for Companies Act/form interpretation.

state_local_dependency.description: Office occupation and stamp consequences depend on the state and instrument.

tasks.fail_closed_note: Foreign or regulated facts require additional evidence outside this standard pack.

tasks.title: File SPICe+ and linked incorporation forms
tasks.user_goal: Submit one coordinated Central incorporation application and linked registrations.
tasks.trigger: The filing pack and valid signatures are ready and any separate name approval is current.
steps: Complete SPICe+ Part B.
Complete linked eMOA/eAOA, INC-9 and AGILE-PRO-S as applicable.
Treat GST as optional unless the classified case is liable.
Select the bank only from the live AGILE-PRO-S options.
Apply DSCs, submit, pay the live-calculated amount and retain SRN/receipt.
tasks.tracking: Track the SRN/transaction status in MCA and preserve every submitted PDF, attachment, notice and payment receipt.
tasks.rejection_handling: Use the resubmission comments; the official FAQ states a maximum of two resubmissions under the cited rule path.
tasks.escalation: Open and track an MCA service request for portal/payment failures; use the CRC/ROC and certifying professional for substantive resubmission or rejection remarks.

state_local_dependency.description: State stamp duty and the optional/state-scoped AGILE integrations are not national obligations.

tasks.fail_closed_note: EPFO/ESIC identifier issuance does not prove contribution liability; t12 handles state integrations and t23 handles unverified money.

tasks.title: Track, cure resubmission, or escalate the incorporation filing
tasks.user_goal: Move the filing to approval without concealing defects.
tasks.trigger: An SRN exists and the application is pending, returned or rejected.

timelines.label: Resubmission response window
timelines.applicability: Use the deadline displayed on the actual notice; no universal number is asserted here.

steps: Read the live status and download the notice.
Map each observation to a corrected field/document.
Have the appropriate signatory/professional re-certify.
Resubmit before the notice deadline and retain the new acknowledgement.
tasks.tracking: Use SRN status and preserve notices, revised documents and acknowledgements as one audit trail.
tasks.rejection_handling: After final rejection, diagnose whether a new name/application or legal correction is required before refiling.
tasks.escalation: Raise and track an MCA service request for technical issues; use the notice/SRN and the published CRC/ROC or certifying-professional route for record-specific issues.

state_local_dependency.description: No state/local escalation is asserted for MCA processing.

tasks.fail_closed_note: The notice-specific deadline controls.

tasks.title: Validate statutory incorporation outputs and linked identifiers
tasks.user_goal: Confirm what was actually issued and preserve authoritative proof.
tasks.trigger: MCA marks the incorporation application approved.
steps: Download and validate the Certificate of Incorporation and CIN.
Preserve the PAN/TAN communication and verify identifiers.
Record EPFO/ESIC registration numbers issued through SPICe+ without inferring contribution liability.
Record the bank application reference.
tasks.tracking: Reconcile names, dates, registered office and identifiers across all outputs.
tasks.rejection_handling: Treat mismatched or missing output as a record-correction/service issue; do not self-correct the authoritative identifier.
tasks.escalation: Use MCA/ROC for incorporation records, Income Tax for PAN/TAN, and EPFO/ESIC for their identifiers.

state_local_dependency.description: This validates Central and linked outputs only.

tasks.fail_closed_note: An identifier is not the same as active bank access, tax liability or social-security contribution liability.

tasks.title: Complete selected-bank KYC and activate the company current account
tasks.user_goal: Obtain a usable company bank account for capital and payroll.
tasks.trigger: A bank application was sent through AGILE-PRO-S and incorporation outputs exist.

timelines.label: Bank activation time
timelines.applicability: Selected bank's current KYC and risk review.

steps: Follow only the selected bank's first-party communication.
Submit company, signatory and beneficial-owner KYC.
Confirm account number, operating mandate and ability to receive/pay funds.
tasks.tracking: Track the bank reference and KYC requests with the bank, not MCA.
tasks.rejection_handling: Correct KYC/beneficial-owner evidence or select another currently available bank route if permitted.
tasks.escalation: Use the bank's grievance route; banking complaint escalation is outside this incorporation pack unless separately researched.

state_local_dependency.description: Bank KYC is a regulated-private dependency.

tasks.fail_closed_note: The MCA-linked request alone is not proof of an active account.

tasks.title: Receive subscription money, verify the office and file INC-20A
tasks.user_goal: Satisfy the commencement condition for a share-capital company.
tasks.trigger: A company with share capital is incorporated and its account can receive subscription money.

timelines.label: INC-20A declaration
timelines.value: Within 180 days of incorporation
timelines.applicability: Companies incorporated after the statutory cut-off and having share capital.

timelines.label: Registered-office verification
timelines.value: Within 30 days of incorporation
timelines.applicability: If not already completed through the incorporation address route, file INC-22 as applicable.

steps: Collect each subscriber's agreed share value into the company account with traceable narration.
Confirm registered-office verification; file INC-22 if the incorporation route did not complete it.
Have a director make the section 10A declaration in INC-20A and obtain professional certification.
Pre-validate the filing because INC-20A is STP and the kit provides no resubmission path.
Submit and retain SRN/acknowledgement before business commencement or borrowing.
tasks.tracking: Track MCA SRNs and reconcile the bank credits to the subscribed-capital table.
tasks.rejection_handling: INC-20A is STP with no resubmission provision: correct evidence before filing; for an acknowledged erroneous record or portal failure, preserve the SRN and use the MCA service-request/ROC/professional correction route instead of promising resubmission.
tasks.escalation: Use MCA help for portal issues and the ROC/professional for section 10A or office-record issues.

state_local_dependency.description: Office occupation/lease and instrument stamp questions remain state-specific.

tasks.fail_closed_note: Do not commence business or borrow before the verified section 10A conditions are met; any live charge is controlled by t23.

tasks.title: Hold the first Board meeting and appoint the first auditor
tasks.user_goal: Create the first governance record and put accountable operating authorities in place.
tasks.trigger: The company is incorporated.

timelines.label: First Board meeting
timelines.value: Within 30 days of incorporation
timelines.applicability: Company governed by section 173.

timelines.label: First auditor appointment by Board
timelines.value: Within 30 days of registration
timelines.applicability: Non-government company; if Board fails, members appoint within the statutory fallback window.

steps: Give notice and hold a quorate first Board meeting under the company's AOA and law.
Record incorporation, registered office, bank mandate, share issuance and statutory records.
Appoint an eligible consenting first auditor within the Board deadline.
Record payroll/TDS authorities without assuming state employment compliance is complete.
tasks.tracking: Maintain signed minutes, attendance and auditor evidence in company records.
tasks.rejection_handling: If the Board misses the auditor deadline, invoke the section 139(6) member-appointment fallback with professional advice.
tasks.escalation: Use a practising company secretary/auditor for defects in meeting or appointment procedure.

state_local_dependency.description: Core Board and auditor duties are Central company law.

tasks.fail_closed_note: This task does not certify every secretarial record or event form.

tasks.title: Issue subscriber share certificates and update statutory records
tasks.user_goal: Evidence founder ownership after subscription money is received.
tasks.trigger: Subscription money and Board authority for issuance are documented.

timelines.label: Certificates to subscribers
timelines.value: Within two months from incorporation
timelines.applicability: Shares allotted to subscribers to the memorandum.

steps: Confirm subscriber payments and allotment details.
Prepare, execute and deliver certificates in the legally applicable form.
Resolve state stamp duty before treating a certificate as complete.
Update the register of members and certificate records.
tasks.tracking: Reconcile certificate numbers, register entries, capital table and bank receipts.
tasks.rejection_handling: Correct ownership/payment inconsistencies through proper company-law procedure; do not overwrite issued records informally.
tasks.escalation: Use a company secretary and the competent state stamp authority for uncertain instruments.

state_local_dependency.description: Stamp duty on share certificates is state/instrument-specific and unresolved in this Central pack.

tasks.fail_closed_note: The two-month Central timing is verified; exact stamp amount and process are not.

tasks.title: Resolve genuine state and local establishment/employment branches
tasks.user_goal: Avoid hiring or operating on a fictional national local-compliance procedure.
tasks.trigger: Registered office and actual employee work locations are known.

fees_duties.label: State/local registrations, taxes, funds, licences and stamp
fees_duties.applicability: Resolve separately for each relevant state/local body.

timelines.label: State/local deadlines
timelines.applicability: No national deadline is asserted.

steps: Identify the competent state/local authorities for every office and employee location.
Check Shops and Establishments, professional tax, trade licence, labour welfare fund, state minimum wages/leave/hours, employment-document rules and relevant stamp instruments.
Record each official portal, trigger, deadline, fee and proof in a state-specific addendum before relying on it.
tasks.tracking: Track each state/local branch independently with official evidence.
tasks.rejection_handling: Use the issuing state's return/rejection process; do not route it through MCA.
tasks.escalation: Use the competent state/local department or a qualified local professional.

state_local_dependency.description: This entire node is a state/local gate.

tasks.fail_closed_note: No state result is claimed by this Central research pack.

tasks.title: Execute the first employee's contract and onboarding record
tasks.user_goal: Create an accurate employment relationship and collect only necessary onboarding data.
tasks.trigger: The company may commence business, the role is genuinely an employee role, and work-location rules are resolved.

timelines.label: Central OSH appointment-letter duty for ordinary establishments
timelines.value: Applies when the OSH Code covers the establishment; the ordinary threshold is 10 or more workers
timelines.applicability: The one-worker demo falls below this Central threshold; state/private contract requirements still require resolution.

steps: Document role, place of work, compensation, wage period, leave/benefits, confidentiality/IP and termination terms consistent with applicable law.
Issue and obtain acceptance of the employment/appointment document.
Collect tax, bank, identity and EPF/ESI history fields using secure handling.
Do not label a contractor as an employee or vice versa to avoid duties.
tasks.tracking: Maintain versioned signed terms and a restricted onboarding checklist.
tasks.rejection_handling: Correct terms before start; obtain specialist advice for classification or state-law conflict.
tasks.escalation: Use employment counsel/qualified state professional for location-specific requirements.

state_local_dependency.description: For a one-worker ordinary services office, the exact employment-document, leave, hours and minimum-wage rules are state-qualified.

tasks.fail_closed_note: No universal Central appointment-letter form is asserted for the one-worker demo.

tasks.title: Establish POSH prevention and the correct complaint route
tasks.user_goal: Give workers a lawful, visible sexual-harassment prevention and redress route.
tasks.trigger: The company establishes a workplace or hires workers.
steps: Implement section 19 employer prevention/assistance duties.
For a workplace below 10 workers, publish the competent District Officer/Local Committee route rather than inventing an Internal Committee.
At 10 or more workers, constitute a compliant Internal Committee and monitor the threshold.
tasks.tracking: Retain policy/training/display evidence and the official district route; protect complaint confidentiality.
tasks.rejection_handling: Correct an invalid committee or route promptly and preserve complainant access to the competent Local/Internal Committee.
tasks.escalation: Use the District Officer/Local Committee and competent state authority for the local route.

state_local_dependency.description: The Local Committee/District Officer identity is local and must be verified for the workplace district.

tasks.fail_closed_note: A generic email or self-appointed committee is not treated as the statutory route.

tasks.title: Configure wage records and run the first payroll
tasks.user_goal: Pay wages on time with an auditable gross-to-net record.
tasks.trigger: The employee works in an active wage period.

timelines.label: Maximum wage period
timelines.value: One month
timelines.applicability: Employee covered by the Code on Wages.

timelines.label: Monthly wage payment
timelines.value: Before expiry of the seventh day of the succeeding month
timelines.applicability: Monthly wage period under the Code on Wages.

steps: Apply the applicable state minimum-wage/leave/hour rules and agreed salary.
Calculate only authorised deductions, including verified TDS/social-security amounts.
Approve payroll, pay by bank and issue a wage statement in the applicable format.
Retain payroll, attendance/leave and payment evidence under the applicable government rules.
tasks.tracking: Reconcile payroll register, bank debit, wage statement and tax/social challans each month.
tasks.rejection_handling: Correct under/overpayment transparently; do not net an unauthorised deduction into a later payroll.
tasks.escalation: Use the appropriate state labour authority/professional for wage-floor or record-format issues.

state_local_dependency.description: The ordinary private services company generally has a state appropriate government for detailed wage rules and minimum wage.

tasks.fail_closed_note: The Central Rules' specific forms are not imposed on this state-sphere demo without state evidence.

tasks.title: Estimate salary income and deduct TDS under the Income-tax Act, 2025
tasks.user_goal: Withhold the correct salary tax for payments from 1 April 2026.
tasks.trigger: Salary is payable in Tax Year 2026-27 or later.

fees_duties.label: Salary TDS amount
fees_duties.applicability: Compute from the employee's estimated salary income, declarations/evidence and current tax law; zero is possible where no tax is estimated.

timelines.label: Deduction time
timelines.value: At the time of salary payment
timelines.applicability: A person responsible for paying income chargeable under salaries.

steps: Verify company TAN and employee PAN.
Estimate the employee's salary income and tax for the tax year using current declarations/evidence.
Deduct at the average rate when salary is paid and adjust lawful excess/shortfall during the year.
tasks.tracking: Version each computation and reconcile it to payroll.
tasks.rejection_handling: Correct PAN/declaration errors and document lawful in-year adjustment.
tasks.escalation: Use a tax professional for regime, perquisite, multiple-employer or cross-border facts.

state_local_dependency.description: Salary TDS is Central income tax.

tasks.fail_closed_note: Do not use legacy section 192 labels for salary paid from 1 April 2026.

tasks.title: Deposit salary TDS, file Form 138 and issue Form 130
tasks.user_goal: Complete the first Central salary-tax remittance and reporting cycle.
tasks.trigger: Salary TDS is actually deducted.

fees_duties.label: Interest for failure to deduct/pay
fees_duties.value: 1% per month or part for delayed deduction; 1.5% per month or part after deduction until payment
fees_duties.applicability: Only on an actual default under Income-tax Act, 2025 section 398.

fees_duties.label: Late Form 138 statement fee
fees_duties.value: INR 200 for each day of continuing delay, capped at tax deductible/collectible
fees_duties.applicability: Only when the statement is delivered after its prescribed due date under section 427.

timelines.label: Ordinary monthly TDS deposit
timelines.value: By the 7th day of the succeeding month
timelines.applicability: Ordinary non-government salary deduction; verify any special March rule in the live calendar before use.

timelines.label: Form 138 quarterly statement
timelines.value: 31 July, 31 October, 31 January and 31 May for quarters 1 to 4
timelines.applicability: Company employer that deducted salary TDS.

timelines.label: Form 130 certificate
timelines.value: By 15 June following the tax year
timelines.applicability: Where salary tax was deducted and deposited.

steps: Create and pay the Income-tax Act, 2025 TAN challan through e-Pay Tax.
Retain challan receipt and reconcile CIN/payment.
File quarterly Form 138 with employee/PAN/challan data and retain acknowledgement.
Review acceptance/rejection and processing; for a discrepancy, prepare an updated FVU and select Upload Type Correction using the original RRR.
Pay statutory interest/late fee before the statement where an actual default exists.
After statement processing, download TRACES-generated Form 130 and issue it to the employee.
tasks.tracking: Use e-Pay Tax payment history, Form 138 View Filed Forms/processing status and TRACES statement, default and certificate status.
tasks.rejection_handling: The Form 138 manual identifies regular/correction upload, FVU-version, TAN, upload-type and RRR mismatches: rectify the specific error, upload the correct FVU and regenerate Form 130 only after corrected processing.
tasks.escalation: Use Income Tax e-filing grievance categories for quarterly-statement, challan/BIN, default or TRACES issues; use TRACES or the Assessing Officer for TAN challan correction where the portal directs.

state_local_dependency.description: Central tax process.

tasks.fail_closed_note: Legacy Form 24Q/Form 16 terminology is superseded for Tax Year 2026-27.

tasks.title: Classify EPF coverage; enrol and remit only if applicable
tasks.user_goal: Separate the issued EPFO identifier from actual establishment/member contribution duties.
tasks.trigger: An employee joins or establishment headcount/coverage changes.

fees_duties.label: Employee and employer EPF contributions
fees_duties.value: Ordinarily 12% employer and an equal employee contribution for a covered member
fees_duties.applicability: Only after establishment coverage and member eligibility are established under the Employees' Provident Funds Scheme, 2026.

timelines.label: ECR/payment
timelines.value: Within 15 days of the close of the month
timelines.applicability: Covered establishment with contributions due under Employees' Provident Funds Scheme, 2026 paragraph 20(1).

steps: Decide establishment coverage: ordinary threshold 20 employees, plus any lawful special/voluntary coverage.
If not covered, record the no-contribution basis and monitor headcount; do not close the MCA-issued code.
If covered, collect prior UAN/membership and current employee data, then apply Scheme 2026 paragraphs 2(f) and 9 before enrolment/linking.
Prepare UAN-based ECR, generate challan, pay and retain proof within 15 days after month close under paragraph 20.
tasks.tracking: Use the current UAN-based employer portal, ECR/TRRN and payment history; use EPFiGMS for unresolved grievances.
tasks.rejection_handling: Use the revamped ECR validation/revision controls for member, wage or return errors; correct UAN/KYC separately and preserve rejected/revised return evidence.
tasks.escalation: Use EPFO employer help/EPFiGMS and the jurisdictional EPFO office.

state_local_dependency.description: EPF is Central; employee location can still affect other employment laws.

tasks.fail_closed_note: Use G.S.R. 525(E), Scheme 2026 paragraphs 9 and 18-20, and S.O. 2702(E); do not use superseded Scheme 1952 paragraphs or the former 20-November scheme checkpoint.

tasks.title: Classify ESI coverage; enrol and remit only if applicable
tasks.user_goal: Separate the issued ESIC identifier from actual establishment/employee contribution duties.
tasks.trigger: A person is employed, establishment headcount changes, or a hazardous occupation/area is notified.

fees_duties.label: ESI contribution rates
fees_duties.applicability: Covered employee in a covered establishment/implemented area.

timelines.label: ESI contribution payment
timelines.value: Within 15 days of the last day of the calendar month
timelines.applicability: Covered employer/employee while saved ESI General Regulation 31 remains operative; recheck before any payment on or after 20 November 2026 or earlier supersession.

steps: Decide establishment coverage: ordinarily 10 or more persons, or a notified hazardous/life-threatening occupation even with one employee, and confirm area/benefit notification.
If establishment coverage applies, locate the current Chapter IV wage-ceiling notification; do not reuse superseded ESI Central Rules rule 50 or the legacy FAQ.

Before or on the first day of employment, register a covered employee on the specified portal under Social Security (Central) Rules, 2026 rule 18 and complete the declaration/Aadhaar update within 30 days.
Apply Rule 19's 3.25% employer and 0.75% employee rates; for a qualifying person with disability apply the employer-share relief in Rule 19(2)-(3).

Use the ESIC employer portal monthly-contribution/challan route and saved General Regulation 31's 15-day deadline; recheck the regulation before a payment on or after 20 November 2026 or any earlier replacement.
If not covered, record the reason and monitor headcount/notification changes.
tasks.tracking: Use employer-portal employee status, monthly-contribution history and challan/payment status.
tasks.rejection_handling: Correct IP identity, date of joining, wage or contribution data through the ESIC portal/office; preserve the error and correction trail.
tasks.escalation: Use ESIC employer help/CPGRAMS and the jurisdictional ESIC office for a written current Chapter IV wage-ceiling determination or a post-savings remittance rule when the Gazette trail is incomplete.

state_local_dependency.description: Coverage also requires the relevant notified geographical/benefit operation; verify against ESIC's current jurisdictional material.

tasks.fail_closed_note: The demo is outside ordinary establishment coverage because it has one person and no identified hazardous notification; its salary is not used to reach that result. If establishment coverage later applies, the current Chapter IV ceiling remains Action Required, and saved Regulation 31 must be rechecked for payments on or after 20 November 2026 or earlier replacement.

timelines.applicability: Person that becomes liable to registration, subject to the Act/notifications.

steps: Classify supply type and aggregate turnover under section 22.
Apply section 23 non-liability and current exemption notifications, then test every section 24 compulsory-registration category; do not stop at turnover.
If GST is selected during incorporation, complete the optional GST fields in AGILE-PRO-S.
Otherwise, when liable, submit REG-01 on the GST portal and complete Aadhaar authentication/verification.
Track ARN; respond to REG-03 with REG-04; preserve REG-06 or REG-05.
tasks.tracking: Maintain turnover/supply monitoring and track ARN/status on GST portal.
tasks.rejection_handling: Answer REG-03 in REG-04 with evidence; treat REG-05 as rejection requiring fact/legal review before a fresh route.
tasks.escalation: Use GST portal help and the jurisdictional tax officer/tax professional.

state_local_dependency.description: Registration thresholds and place-of-supply analysis depend on the states/UTs involved, but GST remains a Central/state integrated tax regime rather than a local licence.

tasks.fail_closed_note: The old general service threshold does not by itself resolve current compulsory triggers for an actual business.

tasks.title: Create the first annual MCA compliance calendar

timelines.label: Financial statements filing
timelines.value: Within 30 days of AGM
timelines.applicability: Ordinary company route; OPC files within 180 days of financial-year closure.

timelines.label: Annual return filing
timelines.value: Within 60 days of AGM
timelines.applicability: Every company; use the current form selected by company class, including MGT-7A only where eligible.

steps: Maintain books and close the first financial year.
Obtain audit and Board approval of financial statements.
Hold the first AGM if applicable.
Use the current MCA form for financial statements and the correct annual-return form for company class; retain SRN and acknowledgement.
tasks.tracking: Calendar deadlines from the actual financial-year close and AGM date; use MCA Track Transaction Status for each SRN and preserve every notice/acknowledgement.
tasks.rejection_handling: Use the actual annual-form status and notice to correct form/classification or attachments; do not transplant the SPICe+ maximum-two-resubmission rule to annual forms, and disclose missed filings rather than backdating.
tasks.escalation: Open and track an MCA service request for technical/status defects; use the auditor/company secretary and ROC for substantive filing defects.

state_local_dependency.description: These are Central company-law filings; state tax/employment calendars remain separate.

tasks.fail_closed_note: The current annual-return form depends on company class; do not assume MGT-7A without confirming status, and route live charges through t23.

steps: Review worker/person count, wages, prior membership, notified geography and hazardous notifications.
Use the current EPF Scheme 2026 and Social Security Rules 2026; do not treat 20 November 2026 as a future switch date for the superseded EPF Scheme 1952 or ESI Central Rules 1950.
Separately recheck saved ESI General Regulation 31 before any payment on or after 20 November 2026 or an earlier replacing regulation.
Create a dated decision and activate the linked Central task before its first deadline.
Leave GST monitoring to t20 and state/local monitoring to t12.
tasks.tracking: Monthly control log with evidence snapshot and next review date.
tasks.rejection_handling: Treat an uncertain or crossed threshold as Action Required; do not wait for a portal notice.
tasks.escalation: Ask the relevant authority/professional for written classification where facts remain ambiguous.

state_local_dependency.description: State/local and GST monitoring are separated into t12 and t20.

tasks.fail_closed_note: A prior no-duty conclusion expires when facts or law change.

Approve and pay only the case-specific amount; retain calculation, SRN and receipt.

portal_journeys.name: MCA21 SPICe+ and company e-filing
portal_journeys.authentication: Registered MCA user; valid DSC and role association where the live form requires it.
portal_journeys.navigation: MCA Services > Company e-Filing; use SPICe+ Part A/Part B and linked forms for incorporation, then INC-20A/INC-22 and current annual forms; use Enquire Fee and Track Transaction Status as preliminary/status controls.
inputs_uploads: AGILE-PRO-S bank, EPFO, ESIC and optional GST data
portal_journeys.submission_proof: SRN, payment receipt, acknowledgement, notice/order and issued certificate/form record.
portal_journeys.tracking_route: MCA Track Transaction Status/SRN after login; preserve notices, acknowledgements, calculations and service-ticket history.
portal_journeys.exception_route: Follow the actual form notice: name defects have rule 9's fifteen-day cure; SPICe+ incorporation has the FAQ's maximum-two resubmissions; INC-20A is STP with no resubmission provision; annual forms use their own status/notice. Open and track a service request for technical defects and use CRC/ROC/professional review for substantive defects.
portal_journeys.access_limitation: Transactional content is login-gated and dynamic; final fees, selectable banks and notice deadlines must be captured from the live case.

portal_journeys.name: Selected integrated bank account activation
portal_journeys.authentication: Bank-specific company/signatory KYC after AGILE-PRO-S referral.
portal_journeys.navigation: Follow only the selected bank's first-party referral/KYC route.
portal_journeys.submission_proof: Bank application/KYC acknowledgement and active account proof.
portal_journeys.access_limitation: No bank is hard-coded because the live AGILE-PRO-S list and product terms are volatile.

portal_journeys.name: Income Tax e-Pay Tax and Form 138
portal_journeys.authentication: Company TAN/PAN login or permitted e-Pay Tax flow with authorised credentials.
portal_journeys.navigation: e-Pay Tax: create TAN challan and select Income-tax Act, 2025 for Tax Year 2026-27 onward; file Form 138 as Regular or Correction with the current RPU/FVU workflow.
portal_journeys.submission_proof: Challan receipt/payment history and accepted regular/correction Form 138 acknowledgement/status.
portal_journeys.tracking_route: e-Pay Tax payment history, View Filed Forms/processing result and TRACES default/certificate status.
portal_journeys.exception_route: Correct the precise FVU version, TAN, upload type or RRR defect; use e-filing grievance categories for statement/challan/default issues and TRACES or the Assessing Officer for TAN-challan correction as directed.
portal_journeys.access_limitation: Login and filing utilities are dynamic; this pack does not state a computed TDS amount.

portal_journeys.name: TRACES Form 130 certificate
portal_journeys.authentication: Registered TAN deductor after Form 138 processing.
portal_journeys.navigation: Use processed statement data to download the system-generated Form 130.
portal_journeys.exception_route: TRACES correction/support route after correcting the underlying statement where necessary.
portal_journeys.access_limitation: Login-gated; exact screens were not publicly inspectable.

portal_journeys.name: EPFO unified employer ECR/UAN portal
portal_journeys.authentication: Employer credentials and authorised signatory; member UAN/KYC data when covered.
portal_journeys.navigation: Register/link an eligible member or prior UAN under Scheme 2026; use the UAN-based revamped ECR validation and conditional revision workflow; generate challan and pay electronically.
portal_journeys.submission_proof: Member/UAN record, accepted or revised ECR, TRRN/challan and payment confirmation.
portal_journeys.tracking_route: ECR/challan/payment history; EPFiGMS at https://epfigms.gov.in/ for grievances.
portal_journeys.exception_route: Use revamped-ECR validation/revision for return data, UAN/KYC correction for member data, and the jurisdictional EPFO office/EPFiGMS for unresolved issues.
portal_journeys.access_limitation: Operational screens are login-gated; legal coverage, membership, rate and due date use G.S.R. 525(E), Scheme 2026 and S.O. 2702(E), not legacy portal reference documents tied to Scheme 1952.

portal_journeys.name: ESIC employer employee-registration and contribution portal
portal_journeys.authentication: Employer credentials linked to the ESIC registration number.
portal_journeys.navigation: For a covered employee, register before or on the day employment starts, complete declaration/Aadhaar data within 30 days, file monthly contribution, and generate/pay challan.
inputs_uploads: Date of joining and wage data
portal_journeys.submission_proof: Insurance/IP number or electronic identity record, submitted contribution, challan and payment confirmation.
portal_journeys.tracking_route: Employer-portal employee, monthly-contribution, challan and payment history.
portal_journeys.exception_route: Correct IP or contribution data through the employer portal/office; use ESIC help/CPGRAMS and the jurisdictional office for unresolved legal or system issues.
portal_journeys.access_limitation: Login-gated; current law is Code section 28 and Rules 18-19, not legacy portal labels. Geographical benefit operation and the current Chapter IV wage ceiling remain case gates. Saved General Regulation 31 supplies the current 15-day deadline only until earlier replacement or the end of its section 164 savings period, so recheck for payments on or after 20 November 2026.

portal_journeys.name: Shram Suvidha common establishment registration
portal_journeys.authentication: Employer registration and digital authentication required by the current portal.
portal_journeys.navigation: For an establishment not already registered under the Social Security Code, submit the common electronic registration in Form I under the applicable operational route.
portal_journeys.submission_proof: Registration certificate or auto-generated/deemed certificate where the rule applies.
portal_journeys.exception_route: Portal help and competent social-security organisation.
portal_journeys.access_limitation: SPICe+ already issues EPFO/ESIC identifiers for new companies; use this common route only after confirming it is required for the actual case.

portal_journeys.name: GST REG-01 registration journey
portal_journeys.authentication: Applicant creates/uses GST portal credentials and completes Aadhaar authentication or alternative verification as prompted.
portal_journeys.navigation: After sections 22-24 classification, use Services > Registration > New Registration; submit REG-01; respond to REG-03 in REG-04; receive REG-06 or REG-05.
portal_journeys.submission_proof: Dated liability decision, ARN and REG-06 registration certificate, or REG-05 rejection order.
portal_journeys.tracking_route: Track Application Status using ARN on GST portal.
portal_journeys.exception_route: REG-04 clarification response and portal/jurisdictional officer help; after REG-05, correct the factual/legal classification before a fresh application.
portal_journeys.access_limitation: Liability classification and exact current uploads depend on the actual supply and live form; turnover alone is not a complete decision.

claims.statement: A lawful-purpose public company may be formed by seven or more persons, a private company by two or more persons, and an OPC by one person.
claims.subject: Company member minima
claims.applicability: Choice of company form under Companies Act section 3.
claims.locator: Companies Act, 2013, section 3(1)(a)-(c).

claims.statement: A public company requires at least three directors, a private company at least two and an OPC at least one; every company must have at least one director satisfying the 182-day India-stay rule for the financial year.
claims.subject: Director minima and residence
claims.applicability: Companies Act section 149, proportionate for a newly incorporated company.
claims.locator: Companies Act, 2013, section 149(1) and first proviso.

claims.statement: Section 7 requires the constitutional documents, declarations and prescribed subscriber/first-director particulars to be filed for incorporation.
claims.subject: Incorporation documents
claims.applicability: Company incorporation.
claims.locator: Companies Act, 2013, section 7(1)(a)-(g).

claims.statement: On satisfactory filing, the Registrar issues a Certificate of Incorporation and allots a Corporate Identity Number.
claims.subject: Incorporation output
claims.applicability: Registrar satisfied with section 7 filing.
claims.locator: Companies Act, 2013, section 7(2)-(3).

claims.statement: SPICe+ and its linked forms use digital signatures of the applicable signatories/professional.
claims.subject: MCA signing
claims.applicability: Electronic incorporation filing.
claims.locator: SPICe+ instruction kit Part II signing/submission workflow; INC-20A kit Part II prerequisites include valid DSC.

claims.statement: Separate SPICe+ Part A permits up to two proposed names and an approved name is reserved for 20 days; an integrated Part A plus Part B permits one proposed name.
claims.subject: Name reservation
claims.applicability: New-company name request.
claims.locator: SPICe+ FAQ, questions 21 and corresponding Part A/Part B name guidance.

claims.statement: Companies (Incorporation) Rules rule 9 routes a new-company name request through SPICe+ and allows resubmission within 15 days to rectify defects before approval or rejection by the Central Registration Centre.
claims.subject: Name-defect resubmission
claims.applicability: SPICe+ name webform returned for rectification under rule 9.
claims.locator: G.S.R. 128(E), substituted Companies (Incorporation) Rules rule 9, Gazette page 28.

claims.statement: The official SPICe+ FAQ lists MOA/AOA, subscriber/director identity and residential evidence, office proof/NOC and a utility bill not older than two months among incorporation inputs.
claims.subject: SPICe+ inputs
claims.applicability: Standard incorporation; exact attachments vary with facts.
claims.locator: SPICe+ FAQ, question 45 and attachments table.

claims.statement: SPICe+ is a single application for name reservation, incorporation, DIN allotment, PAN and TAN, subject to the form's limits and applicability.
claims.subject: SPICe+ integrated outputs
claims.applicability: New company incorporation.
claims.locator: SPICe+ instruction kit, Part I Purpose of the web form, page 2.

claims.statement: New companies apply for EPFO and ESIC registration numbers through SPICe+/AGILE-PRO-S, but the identifiers do not establish contribution liability; classification follows the current Code, EPF Scheme 2026 and Social Security Rules 2026, while contribution transactions use the respective employer portals.
claims.subject: EPFO/ESIC incorporation integration
claims.applicability: New company; ESIC number exception where the area is not implemented as stated by MCA.
claims.locator: SPICe+ FAQ question 39; G.S.R. 525(E); G.S.R. 344(E); current EPFO employer portal and ESIC January 2026 employer-portal manual.

claims.statement: GSTIN application in AGILE-PRO-S is optional, unlike the linked bank-account application.
claims.subject: GST integration
claims.applicability: Incorporation; actual GST liability remains separately classified.
claims.locator: AGILE-PRO-S instruction kit Purpose/description; SPICe+ FAQ questions 40 and 44.

claims.statement: An application to open a bank account is mandatory through AGILE-PRO-S for a new company.
claims.subject: Bank application integration
claims.applicability: New company incorporation.
claims.locator: SPICe+ FAQ, question 40.

claims.statement: The selected bank's current KYC, product terms, activation time and selectable-bank status must be verified after AGILE-PRO-S referral.
claims.subject: Bank activation
claims.applicability: Post-incorporation bank onboarding.
claims.locator: Live bank-specific public instructions were not fixed in this pack.

claims.statement: The official SPICe+ FAQ states that a maximum of two resubmissions is permitted under the cited incorporation rule path.
claims.subject: MCA resubmission
claims.applicability: SPICe+ incorporation application returned for resubmission; not a universal limit for name, INC-20A or annual forms.
claims.locator: SPICe+ FAQ, question 65.

claims.statement: MCA publishes Enquire Fee and Track Transaction Status services and a service-request/grievance route; the incorporation FAQ directs technical and payment defects to a ticket and separates substantive resubmission/rejection remarks for CRC escalation.
claims.subject: MCA tracking and escalation
claims.applicability: MCA filing, payment or status defect; the actual notice and current portal contact control.
claims.locator: MCA Website FAQ questions 15 and 17; SPICe+ FAQ questions 72-74; MCA21 Online Help pages 32-33, service-request creation and ticket status/update/reopen controls.

claims.statement: MCA's incorporation material separates the consolidated Central form, MOA, AOA, PAN and TAN components from state-dependent stamp duty; authorised capital and state affect the calculation, so the public Enquire Fee/live filing result is a case gate rather than a reusable national total.
claims.subject: MCA fee and stamp split
claims.applicability: SPICe+ incorporation calculation; later forms use their own live fee result.
claims.locator: SPICe+ FAQ questions 29-32; official SPICe+ video transcript consolidated-challan and state-stamp passages; MCA Website FAQ question 17 Enquire Fee service.

claims.statement: Although the Central-versus-state component split is verified, exact name, incorporation, post-incorporation and annual amounts are not admitted as reusable fixed totals; they must be recalculated for the live company, capital, state, form and instrument.
claims.subject: Exact MCA fees and stamp duty
claims.applicability: Actual company subtype, capital, state, form and instrument.
claims.locator: SPICe+ FAQ fee workflow and MCA Enquire Fee service; the login-gated final filing calculation and competent state stamp source remain case-specific.

claims.statement: A company must have a registered office within 30 days of incorporation and furnish verification to the Registrar within 30 days in the prescribed manner.
claims.subject: Registered office
claims.applicability: Every company; the SPICe+ FAQ states INC-22 is not required where the registered address is the same as the incorporation correspondence address.
claims.locator: Companies Act, 2013, section 12(1)-(2); SPICe+ FAQ, question 66.

claims.statement: A post-amendment company with share capital may not commence business or borrow until a director files, within 180 days of incorporation, the subscriber-payment declaration and registered-office verification is filed.
claims.subject: Commencement of business
claims.applicability: Company having share capital within section 10A.
claims.locator: Companies Act, 2013, section 10A(1)(a)-(b); INC-20A instruction kit Part I and prerequisites.

claims.statement: The INC-20A instruction kit classifies the webform as straight-through processing, electronically taken on record, and states that there is no provision for resubmission.
claims.subject: INC-20A processing and remediation
claims.applicability: INC-20A filing after the section 10A conditions are actually met.
claims.locator: INC-20A Instruction Kit, Part IV paragraph 4.2, official PDF page 11.

claims.statement: Every company must hold its first Board meeting within 30 days of incorporation.
claims.subject: First Board meeting
claims.applicability: Company under section 173.
claims.locator: Companies Act, 2013, section 173(1).

claims.statement: For a non-government company, the Board appoints the first auditor within 30 days of registration; if it fails, members appoint within 90 days at an extraordinary general meeting.
claims.subject: First auditor
claims.applicability: Non-government company.
claims.locator: Companies Act, 2013, section 139(6).

claims.statement: Certificates for shares allotted to subscribers to the memorandum must be delivered within two months from incorporation.
claims.subject: Subscriber share certificates
claims.applicability: Shares allotted to subscribers.
claims.locator: Companies Act, 2013, section 56(4)(a).

claims.statement: Shops and Establishments, professional tax, trade licence, labour welfare fund, state wage/leave/hour rules and instrument stamp duties must be resolved for the actual state/local jurisdictions; this pack proves no national procedure or amount.
claims.subject: State/local compliance
claims.applicability: Depends on registered office, workplace, employee and instruments.
claims.locator: Deliberate Central-scope boundary; requires competent state/local primary sources.

claims.statement: Official MCA AGILE-PRO-S materials do not support treating professional tax or Shops and Establishments as one national procedure because their descriptions scope them to particular states/Delhi and appear inconsistent on mandatory/optional treatment.
claims.subject: AGILE state integrations
claims.applicability: AGILE-PRO-S state fields during incorporation.
claims.locator: AGILE-PRO-S kit pages 3-4; SPICe+ FAQ questions 41 and 44.

claims.statement: The four labour codes, including the Code on Wages, Social Security Code and OSH Code, were brought into force on 21 November 2025.
claims.subject: Labour-code commencement
claims.applicability: From 21 November 2025, subject to each Code's scope.
claims.locator: Gazette S.O. 5322(E); Ministry of Labour Year End Review; OSH Code India Code enforcement date.

claims.statement: The former blanket proposition that EPF Scheme 1952 and ESI Central Rules 1950 remain the operating scheme/rules until 20 November 2026 is stale: G.S.R. 344(E) superseded the ESI Central Rules on 8 May 2026 and G.S.R. 525(E) superseded EPF Scheme 1952 on 29 June 2026. This does not erase the separate, narrower section 164 savings analysis for ESI General Regulation 31, which neither final instrument expressly superseded.
claims.subject: Superseded social-security transition proposition
claims.applicability: Historical scheme/rule proposition only; section 164 can continue a distinct instrument only until earlier repeal/supersession, one year, and to the extent not inconsistent.
claims.locator: Code on Social Security section 164(2) first proviso; G.S.R. 344(E) opening and rule 1; G.S.R. 525(E) opening and paragraph 1; ESI General Regulation 31 treated separately.

claims.statement: An establishment not already registered under the Social Security Code applies electronically in common Form I on the Shram Suvidha portal; the rule provides certificate issuance within seven days or auto-generation where its conditions are met.
claims.subject: Social Security common registration
claims.applicability: Establishment requiring registration and not already registered; new companies usually receive EPFO/ESIC identifiers through SPICe+.
claims.locator: Social Security (Central) Rules, 2026, rule 5 and Form I registration provisions, official PDF pages 138-139.

claims.statement: Chapter III of the Social Security Code applies to every establishment in which 20 or more employees are employed.
claims.subject: EPF establishment threshold
claims.applicability: First Schedule Part I; other notified/voluntary coverage must be separately checked.
claims.locator: Code on Social Security First Schedule, Part I, Chapter III row.

claims.statement: G.S.R. 525(E) made the Employees' Provident Funds Scheme, 2026 effective on Gazette publication on 29 June 2026 and expressly superseded the Employees' Provident Funds Scheme, 1952 except for prior acts or omissions.
claims.subject: Current EPF scheme
claims.applicability: From 29 June 2026 to establishments within Scheme 2026 paragraph 1(3).
claims.locator: G.S.R. 525(E), opening supersession text and paragraphs 1(1)-(3), Gazette page 66.

claims.statement: Scheme 2026 carries prior members into the new Scheme and requires a non-excluded employee of a covered establishment to become a member from Scheme applicability or joining, whichever is later; S.O. 2702(E) sets the Chapter III wage ceiling at 15,000 rupees per month.
claims.subject: EPF member eligibility
claims.applicability: Covered establishment under Scheme 2026; excluded, exempted and joint higher-wage opt-in cases follow paragraphs 2(f) and 9(3)-(4).
claims.locator: G.S.R. 525(E), paragraphs 2(f), 9(1)-(4), Gazette pages 66 and 68-69; S.O. 2702(E), operative paragraph, Gazette page 2.

claims.statement: Scheme 2026 sets the employer contribution at 12 percent of wages and the employee contribution equal to it, subject to the notified 10-percent classes and other expressly notified adjustments.
claims.subject: EPF contribution rate
claims.applicability: Covered member/establishment under Scheme 2026 paragraph 18.
claims.locator: G.S.R. 525(E), paragraph 18(1)-(4), Gazette pages 75-76.

claims.statement: The employer must pay both contribution shares and applicable charges within 15 days of the close of every month in the manner specified by the Central Board; the current employer portal provides the ECR/payment route.
claims.subject: EPF first remittance
claims.applicability: Covered establishment/member under Scheme 2026 paragraph 20.
claims.locator: G.S.R. 525(E), paragraph 20(1)-(4), Gazette pages 76-77; EPFO employer portal ECR/payment services.

claims.statement: EPFO's employer portal remained live and UAN-based in August 2026, while EPFO's current Revamped ECR page verifies segregation of return and payment, system validations, damages/interest calculation and conditional ECR revision; these transaction mechanics do not replace Scheme 2026 eligibility, rates or due dates.
claims.subject: Current EPFO employer portal
claims.applicability: Covered establishment using the employer portal after legal classification.
claims.locator: EPFO employer home page last updated 19 August 2026; EPFO Revamped ECR page body, key-features list and linked current user manual/FAQ, accessed 28 August 2026.

claims.statement: Chapter IV of the Social Security Code ordinarily applies to establishments with 10 or more persons and may apply to a notified hazardous or life-threatening occupation even where only one employee is employed.
claims.subject: ESI establishment threshold
claims.applicability: First Schedule Part II plus notified area/benefit operation.
claims.locator: Code on Social Security First Schedule, Part II, Chapter IV rows (a)-(b) and proviso.

claims.statement: G.S.R. 344(E) made the Social Security (Central) Rules, 2026 effective on Gazette publication on 8 May 2026 and expressly superseded the Employees' State Insurance (Central) Rules, 1950 except for prior acts or omissions.
claims.subject: Current ESI Central rules
claims.applicability: From 8 May 2026 under Chapter IV of the Social Security Code.
claims.locator: G.S.R. 344(E), supersession list item (iii) and rule 1(1)-(2), official PDF pages 134-135.

claims.statement: Every employee in an establishment to which Chapter IV applies must be insured subject to the Code; the employer must register a not-already-registered employee before or on the day employment begins and complete the portal declaration details under Rule 18.
claims.subject: ESI employee insurance and registration
claims.applicability: Employee in a covered establishment, subject to notified geography/benefit operation and current individual eligibility.
claims.locator: Code on Social Security section 28(1)-(2), official PDF page 29; Social Security (Central) Rules, 2026 rule 18(1)-(6), official PDF page 159.

claims.statement: A current numeric wage ceiling for becoming a Chapter IV member was not located in the verified 2026 primary-source set. S.O. 2351(E) confirms only that an employee who crosses the ceiling after a contribution period begins continues for that period; it does not state the ceiling amount.
claims.subject: Current ESI wage ceiling
claims.applicability: Individual eligibility after establishment/geographical coverage is established.
claims.locator: Code section 2(89); S.O. 2351(E), operative paragraph, Gazette page 2; old ESI Central Rules rule 50 marked superseded by G.S.R. 344(E).

claims.statement: The former 25,000-rupee-versus-no-ceiling disability conflict cannot determine current eligibility because both propositions came from legacy material tied to the superseded ESI Central Rules 1950; neither supplies the missing current Chapter IV ceiling.
claims.subject: Superseded ESI disability wage-ceiling conflict
claims.applicability: Historical guidance only; do not use for current eligibility.
claims.locator: Legacy Rule 50/ESIC FAQ compared with G.S.R. 344(E) supersession text, official Rules 2026 page 134.

claims.statement: For an employee who is a person with disability under either Act named in Rule 19(2), the employer is not required to pay the employer share for up to three years or the period specified by Central Government, and Central Government reimburses that share to the Corporation.
claims.subject: ESI disability employer-share relief
claims.applicability: Qualifying employee with disability in a covered establishment; this does not supply a Chapter IV wage-ceiling amount.
claims.locator: Social Security (Central) Rules, 2026 rule 19(2)-(3), official PDF page 160.

claims.statement: Rule 19 sets the employer contribution at 3.25 percent and employee contribution at 0.75 percent of wages, rounded as specified.
claims.subject: ESI contribution rates
claims.applicability: Covered employer and insured employee under Chapter IV.
claims.locator: Controlling source: Social Security (Central) Rules, 2026 rule 19(1)(a)-(b), official PDF pages 159-160; earlier ESIC institutional publication only corroborates the percentages.

claims.statement: As of 28 August 2026, ESI General Regulation 31 requires payment within 15 days after calendar-month end and remains saved by Code section 164(2): G.S.R. 344(E) superseded the ESI Central Rules, not the General Regulations, and ESIC itself used the saved Regulations after Code commencement. Recheck before a payment on or after 20 November 2026 or any earlier replacement.
claims.subject: ESI first remittance
claims.applicability: Covered employer/employee while General Regulation 31 remains within section 164 savings and is not earlier superseded or inconsistent.
claims.locator: Code section 164(2) first savings proviso; ESI General Regulation 31 amendment in ESIC Circular No. N-12/13/01/2016-P&D; ESIC 18 December 2025 public notice applying saved General Regulation 10-B after Code commencement; G.S.R. 344(E) supersession list excludes the General Regulations.

claims.statement: ESIC's January 2026 employer-portal manual displays employee enrolment, monthly contribution, challan, contribution-history, delay-interest and correction-related controls; legal coverage, rates and employee registration timing are nevertheless governed by the current Code and final Rules 2026.
claims.subject: Current ESIC employer portal
claims.applicability: Covered establishment using the ESIC portal after legal classification.
claims.locator: ESIC employer-portal manual version 1.0 revised 14 January 2026, official PDF page 5; Code section 28; Rules 18-19 pages 159-160.

claims.statement: The OSH Code's ordinary establishment coverage is for establishments having 10 or more workers, other than special sectors such as mines and docks.
claims.subject: OSH Code threshold
claims.applicability: Ordinary private services establishment; special sector definitions and provisions may differ.
claims.locator: OSH Code section 2(1)(v) definition of establishment and Statement of Objects and Reasons paragraph 3(ii); enforcement date 21-11-2025.

claims.statement: Where the OSH Code applies, the employer must issue an appointment letter in the prescribed form on appointment.
claims.subject: OSH appointment letter
claims.applicability: Employer/establishment within OSH Code coverage; not the ordinary one-worker demo.
claims.locator: OSH Code section 6(1)(f).

claims.statement: The Local Committee receives complaints from establishments where an Internal Committee has not been constituted because there are fewer than 10 workers, and complaints against the employer.
claims.subject: POSH complaint route
claims.applicability: Workplace below 10 workers or complaint against employer.
claims.locator: Sexual Harassment of Women at Workplace Act, 2013, section 6(1).

claims.statement: Every employer has section 19 duties including a safe working environment, prescribed displays/awareness and assistance to the Internal or Local Committee and aggrieved woman.
claims.subject: POSH employer duties
claims.applicability: Employer/workplace under the POSH Act.
claims.locator: Sexual Harassment of Women at Workplace Act, 2013, section 19(a)-(h).

claims.statement: No wage period may exceed one month.
claims.subject: Wage period
claims.applicability: Employees to whom Code on Wages applies.
claims.locator: Code on Wages, 2019, section 16.

claims.statement: For a monthly wage period, wages must be paid before expiry of the seventh day of the succeeding month.
claims.subject: Monthly wage timing
claims.applicability: Employee on a monthly wage period under the Code on Wages.
claims.locator: Code on Wages, 2019, section 17(1)(ii).

claims.statement: Deductions from wages may be made only in accordance with the Code on Wages.
claims.subject: Wage deductions
claims.applicability: Wages covered by the Code.
claims.locator: Code on Wages, 2019, section 18.

claims.statement: For salary paid from 1 April 2026, the payer deducts at payment under Income-tax Act, 2025 section 392 at the average rate on estimated salary income, considering prescribed evidence and lawful adjustment.
claims.subject: Salary TDS
claims.applicability: Salary payment in Tax Year 2026-27 onward.
claims.locator: Income-tax Act, 2025 as amended by Finance Act 2026, section 392(1)-(3); Income Tax TDS compliance transition guidance.

claims.statement: A person deducting tax must obtain and quote the tax deduction account number in prescribed challans, certificates and statements.
claims.subject: TAN
claims.applicability: Tax deductor; TAN is also integrated into SPICe+ incorporation.
claims.locator: Income-tax Act, 2025 section 397; SPICe+ instruction kit purpose.

claims.statement: For the ordinary company-employer case, salary TDS is deposited by the seventh day of the succeeding month under the transition rules for Tax Year 2026-27.
claims.subject: Salary TDS deposit
claims.applicability: Ordinary monthly salary TDS; special March/government cases require separate verification.
claims.locator: Income Tax Interplay and Transition FAQ, Rule 218 deposit timing and Tax Year 2026-27 example.

claims.statement: A company employer that deducts salary TDS files quarterly Form 138 by 31 July, 31 October, 31 January and 31 May for quarters one through four.
claims.subject: Salary TDS statement
claims.applicability: Salary tax actually deducted.
claims.locator: Income Tax Form 138 user manual, applicability and due-date table.

claims.statement: Income-tax Act, 2025 section 397(3)(f) permits a correction statement within two years from the end of the tax year in which the statement was due; the Form 138 workflow supports Regular/Correction uploads and identifies FVU-version, TAN, upload-type and RRR mismatches and their rejection cure.
claims.subject: Form 138 correction and rejection cure
claims.applicability: Correction of a Tax Year 2026-27 onward Form 138 statement; pre-2026 periods remain under the old framework.
claims.locator: Income-tax Act, 2025 section 397(3)(f), official PDF page 497; Form 138 User Manual steps 9-16 and rejection list; TDS Compliance FAQ questions 11-12 transition boundary.

claims.statement: Income-tax Act, 2025 section 398 treats failure to deduct/pay as default and charges 1 percent per month or part for delayed deduction and 1.5 percent after deduction until payment; section 427 charges INR 200 per day for late statements, capped at tax deductible/collectible and payable before filing.
claims.subject: Salary TDS default consequences
claims.applicability: Actual salary-TDS deduction/payment or Form 138 filing default from Tax Year 2026-27 onward.
claims.locator: Income-tax Act, 2025 as amended by Finance Act 2026, sections 398(1),(3) official PDF pages 497-498 and 427(1)-(2) official PDF page 529.

claims.statement: Where salary tax was deducted and deposited, the employer issues the TRACES-generated Form 130 by 15 June following the tax year.
claims.subject: Salary TDS certificate
claims.applicability: Salary TDS deduction/deposit and processed Form 138.
claims.locator: Form 130 FAQ; Income-tax Rules, 2025, rule 215 timing.

claims.statement: A GST registration decision must apply CGST Act section 22's aggregate-turnover rule, section 23 non-liability and exemption notifications, and every section 24 compulsory-registration category before using section 25's application route; turnover alone is not a complete classification.
claims.subject: GST registration classification gate
claims.applicability: Before AGILE-PRO-S GST selection and whenever supply, place or turnover facts change.
claims.locator: Central Goods and Services Tax Act, 2017, sections 22, 23, 24 and 25 on the current India Code record.

claims.statement: Official CBIC summary material states a general services registration threshold of 20 lakh rupees, reduced to 10 lakh rupees in named special-category states, but the actual 2026 case still requires current notification and compulsory-trigger classification.
claims.subject: GST service threshold
claims.applicability: Service supplier without a compulsory-registration trigger; state and supply facts matter.
claims.locator: CBIC GST An Update, registration threshold summary, 1 June 2019; current CGST Act section 22 retains notification-sensitive classification.

claims.statement: A person that becomes liable applies within 30 days; the official portal workflow uses REG-01, REG-03 clarification, REG-04 response, REG-05 rejection and REG-06 certificate artifacts.
claims.subject: GST registration workflow
claims.applicability: Person liable or validly seeking registration; exact liability separately classified.
claims.locator: CBIC GST FAQ registration timing; GST portal official forms list; Aadhaar-authentication registration FAQ.

claims.statement: The first annual general meeting must be held within nine months from closure of the first financial year; the AGM chapter does not apply to an OPC in the same way.
claims.subject: First AGM
claims.applicability: Company other than OPC; apply section 122 for OPC.
claims.locator: Companies Act, 2013, sections 96(1) and 122.

claims.statement: A company files adopted financial statements with the Registrar within 30 days of the AGM; an OPC files within 180 days from financial-year closure.
claims.subject: Financial statement filing
claims.applicability: Annual company filing, subject to section 137 provisos.
claims.locator: Companies Act, 2013, section 137(1) and OPC proviso.

claims.statement: Every company files its annual return with the Registrar within 60 days from the AGM or the date on which it should have been held.
claims.subject: Annual return filing
claims.applicability: Every company; exact current form depends on company class.
claims.locator: Companies Act, 2013, section 92(4).
